web_blocks.title: Macro Regime Gate: 10-Distribution-Day Downtrend & Portfolio Cash Floor

web_blocks.html: Broader market conditions argue strongly against deploying scarce cash into marginal setups. As of November 20, 2026, `facts_US_2026-11-20.json` records a Downtrend regime for the S&P 500: only 38.8% of benchmark stocks sit above their 50-day SMA, 46.9% sit above their 200-day SMA, just 3 of 11 sectors hold above their 50-day SMA, and the index carries 10 distribution days over the trailing 25 sessions. At the same time, our consolidated US portfolio holds only $2,540.35 in cash (3.38% of $75,110.60 NAV)—far below the 22.0% Downtrend cash floor. Deploying cash into a 1.42:1 Base R:R / 1.03:1 EV R:R setup violates both valuation discipline and portfolio cash preservation.

book_paragraphs: A clean chart cannot rescue an inadequate reward-to-risk ratio. As of November 20, 2026, AbbVie's price action looks constructive on the surface. The stock closed at $286.20, holding 13.18% above its rising 30-week moving average ($252.88) and 18.04% above its 200-day moving average ($242.45). Daily volatility has compressed into a 5.44% Bollinger band squeeze, and Friday's +0.94% bounce arrived on 1.62 times average volume.

Yet technical analysis does not operate in a vacuum. First, the S&P 500 sits in a confirmed Downtrend with 10 distribution days in 25 sessions and only 38.8% of stocks above their 50-day average (46.9% above the 200-day average). Second, our US portfolio holds just 3.38% cash ($2,540.35 of $75,110.60 NAV) against a 22.0% Downtrend cash floor. When cash is that scarce, every new dollar must clear a strict 1.50:1 asymmetry hurdle.

book_subsections.title: Why Even the $278.20 Support Shelf Fails Our Asymmetry Gate
paragraphs: To test whether patience fixes the trade, we measure upside from a disciplined pullback entry at $278.20—just below the $279.00 50-day average—down to our $252.23 structural stop (which respects the upward-only ratchet above the prior $249.53 stop). That $25.97 per-share risk requires at least $38.96 of Base-Case upside ($317.16+) to clear 1.50:1.

Against our $315.00 DCF Base target, $278.20 support offers only $36.80 of upside, or 1.42:1 reward-to-risk. Against our $305.00 probability-weighted Expected Value, it offers $26.80 of upside, or 1.03:1. Even if ABBV pulls back to support, the math fails our underwriting standard.

Volume patterns confirm institutional patience rather than urgency: Friday's 8.76M–8.77M share session marked 1.62x 30-day average volume right at the $279.88 swing low, yet buyers stopped short of reclaiming the 20-day moving average ($290.44).

book_subsections.title: Multi-Timeframe Tape Walk: Weekly, Daily, and 4-Hour Signals
paragraphs: Walking down from the weekly chart to the 4-hour chart helps separate healthy consolidation from broader market vulnerability. On the weekly timeframe, AbbVie's 30-week simple moving average stands at $252.88 and continues to slope upward, placing the $286.20 close 13.18% above primary Stage 2 support. Weekly RSI sits at 64.57, confirming institutional sponsorship without reaching overbought extremes. On the November 23 TradingView snapshot, the stock printed $287.68 with a 30-week average at $255.58, though our decision ledger remains anchored to the verified November 20 session close of $286.20.

On the daily chart, the 50-day moving average ($279.00) and the 20-day swing low ($279.88) form a well-defined support shelf right below the 10-week EMA ($281.27). Daily RSI has reset to 49.19 and Bollinger bandwidth has tightened to 5.44%, showing that sellers are not liquidating shares aggressively. On the 4-hour chart, RSI stands at 43.24 just beneath its 20-period and 50-period intraday averages near $289.70, reflecting orderly sideways digestion rather than a breakdown.

book_subsections.title: Why Portfolio Cash Scarcity and 10 Distribution Days Override a Stage 2 Chart
paragraphs: Even a constructive Stage 2 chart must pass two higher-level gates before receiving capital: market regime and portfolio liquidity. On November 20, 2026, the S&P 500 sat in a Downtrend regime with 10 distribution days over 25 sessions, only 38.8% of index constituents above their 50-day moving average, and only 46.9% above their 200-day moving average. Just 3 of 11 sectors held above their 50-day averages. In weak breadth environments, breakouts fail at a much higher rate and defensive leaders often get sold last to raise cash.

Equally important, our consolidated US portfolio holds only $2,540.35 in cash out of $75,110.60 total net worth—a 3.38% cash ratio against our 22.0% Downtrend cash floor. When cash is that tight, deploying capital into a stock whose Base reward-to-risk is 1.42:1 at support—and only 0.85:1 at the current $286.20 price—would weaken portfolio resilience for sub-par upside.

book_subsections.title: Historical Lessons: Why Stage 2 Stocks Still Need Valuation Margin
paragraphs: Stan Weinstein's Stage Analysis works best when a stock breaks out of a long Stage 1 base with strong market breadth and an expanding multiple ahead of it. AbbVie has already rallied +31.89% over the past six months and +22.70% over the past twelve months, climbing from a 52-week low of $190.75 to a high of $302.93 before settling at $286.20. Much of the easy post-Humira re-rating has already occurred.

Buying late-inning Stage 2 consolidations when the S&P 500 has logged 10 distribution days in 25 sessions carries asymmetric downside risk. If broad market selling forces institutional funds to trim defensive healthcare winners, ABBV can easily slice through its $279.00 50-day moving average and test the rising 30-week average at $252.88. With our reference stop set at $252.23—respecting the upward-only ratchet above the prior $249.53 level—a $278.20 entry risks $25.97 per share to reach a $315.00 Base target ($36.80 upside, or 1.42:1). That falls short of the 1.50:1 minimum required to commit capital.

Notice also how the 2026-11-20 verified close ($286.20) compares with the live 2026-11-23 TradingView snapshot ($287.68). That +$1.48 difference (+0.52%) does not change the Stage 2 classification, nor does it rescue the valuation math. At $287.68, upside to our $315.00 Base target narrows even further to +9.5%, while downside to the $252.23 stop widens to -12.3%, compressing live CMP reward-to-risk to 0.77:1. Whether measured at $286.20 or $287.68, the tape confirms that waiting for a deeper dislocation is the only prudent posture.

From a tactical standpoint, traders watching ABBV should note the key inflection levels on both sides of the range. Immediate overhead resistance sits at the 20-day moving average ($290.44) and the 52-week high ($302.93), followed by the classic R1 pivot at $309.80. On the downside, initial support sits at the 10-week EMA ($281.27) and 50-day moving average ($279.00), with our reference shelf at $274.00–$278.20 and the classic S1 pivot at $268.93. Until market breadth heals above 50%, any bounce toward $295–$303 faces supply.
